events.title: Hilo: The Holiday Special with Judd Winick
events.description: We are incredibly excited to welcome New York Times bestselling author-illustrator Judd Winick to the store to celebrate the Hilo Holiday Special! Judd will talk about the latest adventure in his bestselling Hilo series, take questions from the audience, and then sign books. This event is free, but you must purchase a copy of Hilo: The Holiday Special from Linden Tree to enter the signing line. Books can be purchased with an event ticket, in person at Linden Tree, or on our website. The decorations are up! The gifts are wrapped! And Hilo and the gang are enjoying some holiday togetherness. Sure, it would be better if the skating pond wasn't blocked off. And if someone wasn't stealing trees from the tree lot. AND if a giant, super grumpy snowman wasn't going around destroying things. But what's a holiday without holiday surprises?! Can Hilo and friends figure out what the snowman wants before D.J.'s big family party?! Packed with family and food, love and laughter (lots of laughter!) — gather around and enjoy all the gifts of the season with Hilo!
events.blurb: Hear Judd Winick talk about the latest adventure in his Hilo series, ask him questions, and get books signed.

events.title: Storytime with Seina Wedlick
events.description: Join us as we welcome local author Seina Wedlick back to the store to celebrate her new picture book, Noor and the Storyteller, about a girl who fills the starry, moonlit sky with magical tales. Every night, Noor listens for the sound of the gong and the storyteller's drum. Gong, Gong, Gong! Tap! Tap! Tap! With each beat, fantastic tales swirl and sway and unfold around her. One night, she waits and waits, but no drumbeat comes her way. Can Noor tap the drum and keep the storyteller's magic alive? Find out in this modern fairy tale about a young Nigerian girl who taps stories on her drum and carries tradition in her heart.
events.blurb: Meet local author Seina Wedlick at Linden Tree Books and hear her read from her new picture book, Noor and the Storyteller.

events.title: Book Launch with Nathan Hale — In conversation with Nidhi Chanani
events.description: We are incredibly excited to welcome New York Times bestselling author-illustrator Nathan Hale to the store to celebrate the launch of Nathan Hale's Hazardous Tales: The Web of War! Nathan will be in conversation with bestselling author Nidhi Chanani. After their conversation, Nathan and Nidhi will battle in an old-fashioned, no-holds-barred Draw-OFF! This event is free, but you must purchase a copy of The Web of War from Linden Tree to enter the signing line. Books can be purchased with an event ticket, in person at Linden Tree, or on our website. In the summer of 1944, the Allied forces carried out the largest seaborne invasion in military history. American, British, and Canadian soldiers took to the skies and the sand, bombarding the beaches of Normandy, France, in the famous operation known as D-Day. This pivotal battle turned the tides against the Nazis, but how did the French find themselves overtaken by enemy forces to begin with? How did Hitler and his Nazi ideology sweep through Germany so quickly? And how did American military service members and civilians, from generals, to war correspondents, to heroic Black soldiers, work together to defeat the Nazi government and bring an end to Hitler's reign of terror? In The Web of War, history is in your hands! Pick your path and unravel the thrilling, shocking, gruesome, and true stories of the Second World War in this all-new hazardous tale.
events.blurb: Meet author-illustrator Nathan Hale at Linden Tree Books and hear him in conversation with author Nidhi Chanani about his new Hazardous Tales book.

events.title: I Am Human: Storytime + Creative Writing Workshop
events.description: Calling All Humans! Join author-illustrator Laura G. Lee for a special I Am Human book launch, storytime, and creative workshop. Laura will begin with a reading of I Am Human and a playful conversation inspired by the book: What does it mean to be human? How are we different from AI—and how do we know? After the reading, participants are invited to join a hands-on writing and drawing workshop, responding to creative prompts through words and pictures, enjoying snacks, and sharing ideas. All ages are welcome. The workshop is especially well suited to older elementary kids, teens, and adults, while younger children are welcome to enjoy the story time portion with their families. Workshop RSVPs are encouraged so we can prepare enough materials.
events.blurb: Hear Laura G. Lee read I Am Human, then join a playful conversation about what it means to be human.

events.title: Book Launch with Lily Berlin Dodd — In conversation with Misa Sugiura
events.description: We're excited to welcome New York Times bestselling author Lily Berlin Dodd back to the store to celebrate the launch of the second book in her Aerimander Chronicles series, The First Flame! Lily will be in conversation with author Misa Sugiura. With Eva locked away in Byrdhaven and Rubi missing, all Dusty can do is avoid capture and (attempt to) sleep through his nightmares in the wake of Cal's death. When fate leads Dusty back to the Lockwood Inn, he overhears the next stage of Eoin Parnassus' sinister plans for aerimanders, and knows he must do everything in his power to stop it. Dodging strict nuns, wanted posters, seasickness, altitude sickness, a clockwork army, and a perilously evil clown on the way, Myrnie, Eva, and Dusty are willing to fight to the ends of the Earth--or at least the edges of their map--to stop Eoin Parnassus, Director of Kingdom Secrets. But Rubi is hiding a shocking truth and Parnassus may pose an even bigger threat than they could ever have imagined. Who can be trusted when secrets lurk around every corner of the Kingdom?
events.blurb: Hear Lily Berlin Dodd talk with author Misa Sugiura about The First Flame, the second book in her Aerimander Chronicles series.

events.title: Storytime with Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon
events.description: Join us as we welcome Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon to celebrate their empowering new picture book, No Legs, No Limits, inspired by Kanya's childhood and her journey to finding her voice, independence, and freedom on a skateboard. Kanya Sesser was born without legs, but that doesn't mean she has limits! Sometimes I still fall. But I never give up. I make things work for me. Because I'm strong. Because I'm free. Because I have NO limits. Kanya Sesser has spent her life sharing the message that no matter what life deals you, you can do anything. In this picture book based on her childhood, she tells the story of how she first learned to stand up for herself, both on a skateboard and in life. When people grab her wheelchair, to push her to class or onto the bus after school, she's too shocked and too sad to say no. The people around her don't understand that she moves herself. But when she rides a skateboard for the first time, she experiences a new sense of freedom and joy, and she finally finds her voice.
events.blurb: Meet authors Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon at Linden Tree Books and hear their picture book No Legs, No Limits, inspired by Kanya's childhood and her skateboarding journey.

events.title: Middle Grade Book Club: The Wish Ring Cipher
events.description: It's the next meeting of our middle grade book club for ages 9+! The club is led by bookseller extraordinaire Lorilee. We hope to introduce interested readers to amazing new books and the opportunity to talk about them in a fun, relaxed group setting. This month's book is The Wish Ring Cipher by Alexandra Ott, a fast-paced adventure novel filled with puzzle-solving, a hint of magic, and new school fears. Please email lorilee@lindentreebooks.com to RSVP. Emma Avery has always loved solving puzzles and codes, and now that she's processing a recent autism diagnosis and facing down seventh grade at a new school, they're even more important to her. Then Emma meets Nate Lin. He's popular and funny and... loves codes, too. He introduces Emma to the Codebreakers, a group of his friends dedicated to cracking codes that have been discovered in the ruins of a nearby ghost town, which are believed to lead to magical objects. But they're not the only ones on the hunt, and when their sinister rivals close in on an object that grants unlimited wishes, the Codebreakers must race to beat them to it before they use it for dark magic.
events.attendanceNote: For readers ages 9 and older. Email the bookstore to RSVP using its events calendar.
events.blurb: Talk about The Wish Ring Cipher with fellow readers ages 9 and up at a middle grade book club led by bookseller Lorilee.

events.title: Facing Reality Without Losing Your Peace of Mind

events.title: ESL Classes with Evergreen Valley College (EVC) 502: Listening & Speaking
events.description: ESL Listening & Speaking 1 - This is a non-credit, high-beginning level ESL course. Students will learn to pronounce basic words accurately, communicate effectively, understand and use basic grammar structures, and build their foundational vocabulary. To Enroll, You Must: Complete and pass the Self-Guided Computer Assessment. This is not a test—it's simply an assessment to help us place you in the most appropriate ESL class based on your current English level. To ensure accurate results, the GSP should be completed independently and in a quiet setting, without assistance from others. Submit the registration form. To schedule your assessment appointment, send an email to marcela.guevara@sjlibrary.org. ESL 502 Course Information: Starts: August 25, 2026; Ends: December 10, 2026; Class Days: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday; Time: 5:15 PM – 6:45 PM; Instructor: TBD. We will assist you with the application and registration processes in person at the Educational Park Branch Library. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: We will assist you with the application and registration processes in person at the Educational Park Branch Library. Space is limited.
events.blurb: Practice pronunciation, basic grammar, and vocabulary in this high-beginning ESL listening and speaking class.

events.title: Baby Lapsit Storytime

Baby Lapsit invites newborns, infants, babies, and their caregivers to learn together by strengthening their relationship with each other through stories, songs, bounces, tickles, rhymes, books, and play. After Storytime concludes, we invite you to Stay & Play! The Storytime librarian will join in the fun with special toys, giving babies and parents time to connect. Lapsit Storytime: 11:00 - 11:30 am; Stay & Play: 11:30 am - 12:00 pm. Please note that this will be an indoor program. Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. Free. Attendance limits follow SJPL guidelines.

events.title: Music and Movement in Vietnamese and English and Craft / Múa Hát Song Ngữ Anh
events.description: Bilingual Music and Movement in English and Vietnamese is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities both in English and Vietnamese. Music and Movement is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! Following the Storytime, kids will learn to make a simple and creative craft to take home! We host Vietnamese Storytime and Craft every Friday, plus a special bilingual session on the fourth Tuesday of each month. Free. No registration is required. Please note that this will be an indoor program. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Múa hát song ngữ bằng tiếng Anh và tiếng Việt được thiết kế để phù hợp với nhiều lứa tuổi. Chúng tôi mong muốn mời cả gia đình cùng tham gia vào các hoạt động này để cùng hát các bài đồng dao, cùng vận động ngón tay và cùng nhảy múa vui vẻ. Âm nhạc và nhảy múa là một trải nghiệm thú vị và giúp cho cả gia đình tương tác tốt hơn, thúc đẩy niềm vui học tập cho trẻ em ở mọi lứa tuổi. Mọi người đều được nhiệt liệt chào đón tại chương trình này. Sau phần kể chuyện, các bé sẽ được hướng dẫn làm một món thủ công đơn giản và sáng tạo để mang về nhà! Thứ Sáu hằng tuần có hoạt động kể chuyện và thủ công tiếng Việt; riêng thứ Ba tuần thứ tư hằng tháng sẽ có chương trình kể chuyện song ngữ đặc biệt. Chương trình hoàn toàn miễn phí và không cần phải đăng ký trước.
events.blurb: Sing, dance, and play along with bilingual English and Vietnamese songs and early literacy activities.

events.title: 1-on-1 Tech Help / Asistencia Tecnológica
events.description: Get free one-on-one support with everyday tech questions. Our Tech Mentor assistance includes, but is not limited to, basic smartphone, tablet, and computer help; setting up and using email; downloading and using apps; making video calls (Zoom, FaceTime, Google Meet, etc.); browsing the internet (search engine basics, making simple searches, etc.); navigating the SJPL website and digital resources; how to use the 311 app. Please note: Tech Mentor support is limited to basic technology questions. Appointments are recommended. To make an appointment, call (408) 808-3033 or email Marlene Sanchez at marlene.sanchez@sjlibrary.org. Priority will be given to patrons with appointments. Nuestra asistencia de Tech Mentor puede incluir, pero no se limita a: ayuda básica con teléfonos inteligentes, tabletas y computadoras; configurar y usar el correo electrónico; descargar y usar aplicaciones; hacer videollamadas (Zoom, FaceTime, Google Meet, etc.); navegar por internet (conceptos básicos de motores de búsqueda, hacer búsquedas simples, etc.); navegar el sitio web y los recursos digitales de SJPL; cómo usar la aplicación 311. Ten en cuenta: el apoyo de Tech Mentor se limita a preguntas básicas de tecnología. Se recomienda hacer una cita. Para hacer una cita, llame al (408) 808-3033 o envíe un correo electrónico a Marlene Sánchez a marlene.sanchez@sjlibrary.org. Se dará prioridad a los usuarios con cita.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one help with everyday tech questions from a volunteer at Hillview Library.

events.title: Infant & Toddler Storytime
events.description: Come join us every Tuesday for Infant & Toddler Storytime! Infant & Toddler Storytime invites babies and their caregivers to learn together by strengthening their relationship with each other through stories, songs, bounces, tickles, rhymes, books, and play. After Storytime concludes, we invite you to Stay & Play! The Storytime librarian will join in the fun with special toys, giving babies and parents time to connect. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Free. Attendance limits follow SJPL guidelines.
events.blurb: Sing, bounce, and read along with your baby at Infant & Toddler Storytime.

events.title: Día de Los Muertos: Painting / Pintando Calaveras
events.description: Let's Celebrate Day of the Dead! Stop by the Hillview Library and decorate a calavera to celebrate this beautiful tradition. Calavera and painting supplies will be provided. Supplies are limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis. ¡Celebremos el Día de los Muertos! Visita la biblioteca Hillview y decora una calavera para celebrar esta hermosa tradición. Nosotros proporcionaremos las calaveras y los materiales para pintarlas. Los materiales son limitados y estarán disponibles por orden de llegada.
events.attendanceNote: Calavera and painting supplies will be provided. Supplies are limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis.
events.blurb: Paint and decorate a calavera at Hillview Library for Day of the Dead, with supplies provided while they last.

events.title: ESL Classes with Evergreen Valley College (EVC) - ESL 501: Reading & Writing 1
events.description: Develop your English language skills by practicing speaking, listening, reading, writing, vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Do you want to build your English language skills and your confidence? This beginning non-credit ESL course is free! ESL 501 Reading & Writing 1. What will you learn in this class? This is a non-credit, high-beginning-level integrated ESL skills course emphasizing basic reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary. Students will learn to comprehend frequently used words in context, use learned phrases and sentences to express ideas in basic writing, understand basic grammar structures, and read simplified material. Course Information: Starts: August 25, 2026; Ends: December 10, 2026; Meeting Days: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday; Time: 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM; Instructor: Michelle N. Henninger. Before the classes start, you must complete a Guided Self-Placement (GSP). This is not a test—it's simply an assessment to help us place you in the most appropriate ESL class based on your current English level. We will assist you with the application and registration process in person at the Edenvale Branch Library. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited.
events.blurb: Practice speaking, listening, reading, writing, vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar in a free beginning non-credit ESL 501 Reading & Writing 1 class with Evergreen Valley College.

events.title: Family Storytime + Stay & Play
events.description: Storytime is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities. Storytime is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of reading and learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! After storytime, families can Stay & Play with a variety of toys in the Children's Area. Free, with limited capacity. Please note that this will be an indoor program. Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. San José Public Library Storytimes are in alignment with the City's Education and Digital Literacy Initiative.
events.attendanceNote: Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis.
events.blurb: Bring the whole family to sing songs, share stories and rhymes, and try fingerplays and movement activities at Alviso Library.

events.title: Mahjong for Beginners
events.description: Seniors who are interested in learning the basics of Chinese Mahjong or need a refresher are welcome to register for this program. You'll learn while playing the game: How to set up the game tiles and understand them; The flow of the game; How to make sets during the game; How to win it. Learning Mahjong improves cognitive function, helps reduce stress and creates a sense of community. You will also learn strategy, strengthen communication skills, and build a sense of community. Registration required for Mahjong players. Must arrive on time. Those on the waitlist will be considered for no-show spots. Late arrivals will be moved to the waitlist. Other games in the room do not require registration, and may change as needed.
events.blurb: Learn the basics of Chinese Mahjong, or refresh your memory, in a seniors program at Berryessa Library on Tuesday afternoon.

events.title: Asistencia tecnológica y ayuda personalizada
events.description: ¿Estás cansado de no poder hacer cosas tecnológicas por ti mismo? ¿Cansado de esperar a que los miembros de tu familia te ayuden o hagan las cosas por ti? ¡Ahora puedes aprender a hacer todo eso por ti mismo! Tenemos personas pacientes y serviciales disponibles para ayudarte a aprender cualquier tema relacionado con la tecnología. Nunca es tarde para aprender a usar la tecnología. ¡Solo llámanos! La biblioteca te brindará apoyo para: Abrir una cuenta de correo electrónico; Conectarse a un hotspot/Wifi; Usar Chromebooks/computadoras; Usar Zoom; Encontrar e inscribirse en clases de la biblioteca; Obtener una tarjeta de la biblioteca; Reservar materiales; Usar aplicaciones de la biblioteca; Teléfono móvil; Buscar en internet. Este es un programa presencial organizado en la Sucursal de la Biblioteca Latinoamericana. El personal de la biblioteca o un voluntario estarán allí para guiarte en todo, pero serás tú quien controle la computadora. Si no puede asistir a su cita, llame y cancele. Se dará prioridad a los clientes que no falten a sus citas. Gratis. Se requiere registro. Para registrarse, llame al (408) 294-1237.
events.blurb: Practice doing tech tasks yourself with personalized, Spanish-language help at the Biblioteca Latinoamericana, so you can stop waiting on family for help.

events.title: Bridge Card Game
events.description: Bridge is great exercise for your brain! This Bridge program is designed for adults who are passionate about Bridge and are looking to enhance their game with regular practice and social interaction. The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming, making it an ideal setting to engage with fellow Bridge enthusiasts and to refine your strategies. Participants should be familiar with Bridge terminology and have experience in playing the hand as instructions or assistance will not be provided. Free. Seating is limited; registration required. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Cambrian Library!
events.blurb: Play bridge with fellow adults who enjoy the game, with regular practice and social interaction.

events.title: Reading Partners One-on-One Reading Tutoring
events.description: Free Reading Help for Students in Grades 1–3. Recommended for students in 2nd and 3rd grade. Give your child extra support to become a stronger, more confident reader! Reading Partners provides free one-on-one reading tutoring with trained volunteer tutors. Students meet twice a week for 45-minute sessions and receive personalized, research-based reading support. Program Dates: September 21, 2026 – May 28, 2027. Space is limited, and applications are reviewed to determine if the program is a good fit for your child. Apply Online — It's Free! Ayuda de lectura gratis para estudiantes de 1.º a 3.º grado. Recomendado para estudiantes de 2.º y 3.º grado. ¡Brinde a su hijo/a apoyo adicional para que se convierta en un lector más seguro y exitoso! Reading Partners ofrece tutoría de lectura individual y gratuita con voluntarios capacitados. Los estudiantes se reúnen dos veces por semana en sesiones de 45 minutos y reciben apoyo personalizado de lectura basado en investigaciones. Fechas del programa: 21 de septiembre de 2026 – 28 de mayo de 2027. El espacio es limitado y las solicitudes serán revisadas para determinar si el programa es adecuado para su hijo/a. Solicite en línea — ¡Es gratis! Hỗ trợ đọc MIỄN PHÍ cho học sinh lớp 1–3. Khuyến khích dành cho học sinh lớp 2 và lớp 3. Hãy giúp con quý vị nhận thêm sự hỗ trợ để trở thành một người đọc tự tin và thành công hơn! Reading Partners cung cấp hỗ trợ đọc một kèm một hoàn toàn miễn phí với các tình nguyện viên đã được đào tạo. Học sinh tham gia hai buổi mỗi tuần, mỗi buổi 45 phút và nhận được sự hỗ trợ đọc cá nhân dựa trên nghiên cứu. Thời gian chương trình: Ngày 21 tháng 9 năm 2026 – ngày 28 tháng 5 năm 2027. Số lượng chỗ có hạn và các đơn đăng ký sẽ được xem xét để xác định chương trình có phù hợp với con quý vị hay không. Đăng ký trực tuyến — Hoàn toàn MIỄN PHÍ!
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited, and applications are reviewed to determine if the program is a good fit for your child.
events.blurb: Bring your 2nd or 3rd grader for free one-on-one reading tutoring with trained volunteer tutors from Reading Partners.

events.title: Resume & Cover Letter Workshop
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: A well-crafted resume and cover letter are vital tools for helping you stand out to potential employers. Join an SJPL Works Business & Career Librarian to learn the essential elements of a successful resume and cover letter. This workshop will include how to highlight your accomplishments and transferable skills in your resume, and what to include and what not to include in your cover letter. No registration required. Parking validation for the garage at 88 S. 4th Street will be provided at the program. E-newsletter Signup: Get the inside scoop on business and career resources at SJPL. events.blurb: Learn the essential elements of a strong resume and cover letter from an SJPL Works Business and Career Librarian.

events.title: Educational Park Art Club
events.description: This week, in celebration of Native American Heritage Month, we'll learn about Frank Buffalo Hyde, an Onondaga Beaver Clan artist. After, we'll take what we've learned to create art of our own! Join us every Tuesday as we learn about an artist or art style, then make art of our own. Recommended for ages 5-12. November Events: November 3 - Frank Buffalo Hyde (drawing); November 10 - Rangoli (Diwali craft); November 17 - Theresa Secord (weaving); November 24 - Jaune Quick-to-See Smith (map art). Free. Registration not required.
events.blurb: Learn about Onondaga Beaver Clan artist Frank Buffalo Hyde, then make your own art inspired by his work.

events.title: After-School STEaM
events.description: Drop in on Tuesday afternoons at 4:30 p.m. for a new STEaM adventure every week. Active engagement with STEaM promotes academic success. The topic list is subject to change; please check back or call the branch for up-to-date details. Suggested ages vary; please refer to individual program descriptions. Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Aug 18 - The Science of Soap: Floating Drawing & Pepper Experiment. Participants will learn about the properties of soap, how it cleans and why that's important by creating their own floating drawings and playing with adhesion and repulsion properties of pepper and soap. Aug 25 - Logic Games. Work individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles. Please note that the Mental Math: Multiplication program has been rescheduled for Sept 22 and the other math topics have moved accordingly. Sept 1 - Marble Run Fun. Harness the force of gravity as you create your own marble run. Sept 8 - Lego Engineering Challenge (please note topic change). In this workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up. Volcanoes (will be rescheduled at a later time). Learn about the different types of volcanoes and create your own eruption with common household ingredients. Sept 15 - Spike Robotics Code Quest. Learn to code a pre-built Lego Spike robot to move around and collect components using a block-based coding language similar to Scratch. Sept 22 - Mental Math: Multiplication. Children have the opportunity to learn and practice multiplication skills with a focus on understanding how multiplication works and is related to addition. Oct 6 - Wind Turbine Engineering. In this hands-on workshop, participants will build their own working wind turbines using everyday household items. Through fun, interactive experiments, they will test different designs and observe the impact of tweakable variables on performance. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Oct 13 - Paper Rockets. Learn what makes rockets fly high and far! Then join us in making a rocket of your own that can fly the furthest! Participants will learn about propulsion, then create their own rockets. Oct 20 - Properties of Water (Science from Scientists). Participants will explore cohesion, adhesion and surface tension through a series of simple activities that encourage them to investigate and make observations about the unique properties of water. Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Children younger than age 9 must be accompanied by an adult caregiver during this program. Oct 27 - TBA; Nov 3 - Learn About Aerodynamics Through Paper Planes. In this high-flying workshop, participants will build different types of paper planes and learn concepts of aerodynamics and the impact of plane design through fun and interactive experiments. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Nov 10 - Ozobot Maze Runner. Teach your Ozobot to navigate a maze using simple color codes. Nov 17 - Logic Games. Work individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles. Nov 24 - TBA; Dec 1 - Let's Build Parachutes. In this workshop, participants will build parachutes of different shapes, sizes and materials, and observe the impact of their design. They will participate in fun parachute drops with different loads while learning the science behind parachute design. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Dec 8 - Lego Engineering Challenge. In this workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up.
events.attendanceNote: Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Children younger than age 9 must be accompanied by an adult caregiver during this program.
events.blurb: Drop in on Tuesday afternoons for a weekly hands-on STEaM activity at Almaden Library, with topics that change from week to week.

events.blurb: Recibe ayuda para crear tu currículum y buscar oportunidades de empleo.

events.title: Social Workers in the Library Drop-In Hours
events.description: Advice | Information | Referral. Social Workers in the Library offers free social service information and referrals*. Our staff can meet with you, approach your needs without judgement, and help you find where to go for shelter, food, showers, mental health services, legal help, and more. Free. No registration required. *Disclaimer: SJPL's Social Work in the Library does not establish a social worker-client relationship. SJPL does not offer case management or extensive follow-up services. We will try our best to get you connected to any resource we know of that could suit your needs. Tư Vấn / Thông Tin / Giới Thiệu Nhân Viên Xã Hội trong Thư Viện cung cấp miễn phí thông tin về những dịch vụ xã hội và giới thiệu. Nhân viên của chúng tôi có thể gặp gỡ bạn, tiếp cận với nhu cầu của bạn mà không đánh giá, và giúp bạn tìm những nơi để đến trú ẩn, thực phẩm, tắm rửa, những dịch vụ sức khoẻ tâm thần, trợ giúp pháp lý, và nhiều hơn nữa. Miễn phí. Không bắt buộc phải đăng ký. Từ chối trách nhiệm: Nhân Viên Xã Hội của SJPL trong Thư Viện không thiết lập mối quan hệ giữa một nhân viên xã hội và khách hàng. SJPL không cung cấp quản lý các trường hợp hoặc dịch vụ theo dõi mở rộng. Chúng tôi sẽ cố gắng hết sức để kết nối bạn với bất kỳ nguồn nào chúng tôi biết có thể phù hợp với nhu cầu của bạn. Asesoramiento | Información | Referencia. Este programa ofrece información y referencias de servicios sociales gratuitos. Nuestro personal puede reunirse con usted, abordar sus necesidades sin juicio y ayudarle a encontrar dónde ir para obtener refugio, comida, duchas, servicios de salud mental, ayuda legal y más. Gratis. No se requiere registro. *Aviso: El Trabajo Social en la Biblioteca de SJPL no establece una relación de Trabajador Social-Cliente. SJPL no ofrece gestión de casos ni servicios de seguimiento extensos. Haremos todo lo posible por conectarte con cualquier recurso que conozcamos y que pueda satisfacer tus necesidades.
events.blurb: Drop in to talk with a social worker and get free social service information and referrals.

events.title: Math Buddies
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Math Buddies provides students in grades K-3 with an opportunity to improve their math skills by working one-on-one with a volunteer. At Math Buddies, volunteers sit with participating children for an individual, 15-20-minute tutoring session. Volunteers may help participants complete math homework assignments or math worksheet(s) provided by Math Buddies volunteers. Math Buddies creates a positive learning experience for students who may be struggling with math or lack confidence as math students. Free. Pre-registration not required. However, tutoring sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis, and the availability of sessions may be limited depending on the number of volunteers and/or participating children.

events.blurb: Join teens ages 13-18 to plan library activities and build leadership skills with the Teens Reach youth council.

events.title: ELL Advanced English: Writing Club
events.description: English Language Learners (ELL) can practice basic writing skills in English with our tutor in a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners. Sessions take place on the 1st and 3rd (& 5th, if applicable) Tuesdays. Topics may include creating simple sentence structures, learning some basic grammar, and building up to writing a simple paragraph. Suggested for high beginners up to advanced English language learners. Space is limited and registration is required. Please stop by the Vineland Library or call us at (408) 808-3000 to register. Vineland's English Learning series: ELL Beginning English: A beginner program for learners with limited English skills; approximately levels 0-2; ELL Grammar and Vocabulary Club: An intermediate program for learners that know some English but want to learn more complex English; approximately levels 2-3; ELL Conversation Club: An advanced program for learners to practice speaking and listening while also learning about American culture and idioms; approximately levels 3-4; ELL Writing Club: A program where high beginners to advanced level English language learners can learn and practice their English writing skills; approximately levels 2-4.

events.title: Homework Coaching with Delaney
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Need homework help? Students in kindergarten through 5th grade can meet with volunteer Homework Coach Delaney in the Children's Room to get homework support. Students must have assigned homework to work on to participate in a session. Homework Coaches can help look up and explain concepts covered on assigned homework, support students as they work through their assignments, check work, provide a set time to work on homework, and redirect focus as needed. Free, with limited capacity. The homework coach can work with up to 2 students at a time but can take new students if others finish their work early.
events.blurb: Students in kindergarten through 5th grade can bring assigned homework to the Children's Room and work through it with volunteer coach Delaney.

events.title: 3D Printing One-on-One Appointment
events.description: Need help with 3D printing or looking for guided, hands-on experience? This session is ideal for beginners seeking practical experience, guided support, and confidence in using 3D printing technology. This is also a good opportunity for those who attended our 3D Design & Printing workshop and now want to try their hands at it. Participants will have the opportunity to print a simple model under supervision. If you do not have a design, you may choose a free design from Thingiverse or a similar site. All designs are printed in a single color of PLA - filament color at the discretion of the program lead. Designs must print in 1 hour 45 minutes - if you're not sure how long your design will take to print, email cz.sjpl@sjlibrary.org. SJPL reserves the right to refuse any print request. All designs must be compatible with the Creality K1C printer and have a print time of under 45 minutes. Final approval of printability will be determined by the program lead. One appointment per month per person.
events.attendanceNote: One appointment per month per person. The library lists conflicting print-time limits (45 minutes and 1 hour 45 minutes). Confirm your design's limit with Calabazas Library at cz.sjpl@sjlibrary.org.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one, hands-on guidance with 3D printing at Calabazas Library, a session aimed at beginners wanting practical experience.

events.title: Bilingual Toddler Storytime / Tiempo de Cuentos & Stay and Play
events.description: Bilingual Toddler Storytime is designed for toddlers to engage in early literacy activities such as stories, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement. While the program is geared toward children ages 1–3, all children ages 0–5 are welcome to attend. After Storytime concludes, families are invited to Stay & Play. For 30 minutes following Storytime, special age-appropriate toys will be available for children and caregivers to continue the fun together: Storytime: 11:30 a.m. to noon; Stay & Play: noon to 12:30 p.m. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Tiempo de Cuentos & Stay and Play: Tiempo de Cuentos está diseñado para niños pequeños e invita a toda la familia a participar en actividades de alfabetización temprana, como cuentos, rimas, juegos con los dedos y actividades de movimiento. Después de que concluya el Tiempo de Cuentos, las familias están invitadas a quedarse y jugar. Durante 30 minutos después del Tiempo de Cuentos, habrá juguetes especiales y apropiados para cada edad disponibles para continuar la diversión. Tiempo de cuentos: 11:30 a.m. - 12:00 p.m.; Stay & Play: 12:00 p.m. - 12:30 p.m. Este programa ha sido diseñado en alineación con los Estándares de Calidad de la Educación Infantil.
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and play with your toddler during this bilingual early literacy storytime.

events.title: Make & Decorate Sugar Skulls
events.description: Get ready for Día de los Muertos by making a sugar skull! In this multi-session program, participants will learn to make and then decorate sugar skulls using traditional and modern materials. In the first session, using a special sugar mixture and premade molds, we'll create the parts needed for a sugar skull. In the next session, after the sugar skulls have cured, we'll connect the sugar skull pieces and decorate them with colored frosting, foil, sequins, and more! Once decorated, the sugar skulls will be ready to display on your home altar or our community ofrenda. Please note: creating sugar skulls is a multi-day process. Participants will not be able to finish their skulls in one session and should plan to return for the second session to decorate skulls. Session 1: Sunday, November 1, 11:00 AM - 12:30 PM*; Session 2: Tuesday, November 3, 3:30 PM - 5:30 PM. *This program session will take place before the library opens to the public; participants will enter our community room through the doors adjacent to the parking lot. **Sugar skulls not claimed after the program will be discarded. ¡Haz & decora tu propia Calaverita de Azúcar! ¡Ven a celebrar el Día de los Muertos creando una calaverita de azúcar muy especial! En este divertido programa de varias sesiones, aprenderás a hacer y decorar calaveritas usando materiales tradicionales y modernos. En la primera sesión, usaremos una mezcla especial de azúcar y moldes para formar las piezas de la calaverita. En la siguiente sesión, cuando ya estén listas y duritas, uniremos las piezas y las decoraremos con papel de colores, lentejuelas, pintura y mucho más. Al final, podrás llevarte tu calaverita para ponerla en tu altar en casa o en la ofrenda de la comunidad. Importante: Las calaveritas necesitan varios días para estar listas, así que no podrás terminar todo en una sola sesión. ¡Planea regresar a las siguientes para decorarlas! Sesión 1: Domingo, 1 de noviembre, 11:00 - 12:30 PM; Sesión 2: Martes, 3 de noviembre, 3:30 - 5:30 PM.
events.blurb: Make and decorate your own sugar skull with traditional and modern materials in a multi-session Día de los Muertos program.

events.title: Diwali Craft for Kids
events.description: Children and their caregivers are invited to join us for a fun drop-in craft in celebration of Diwali. Rangoli is a traditional Indian folk art for the floor or a tabletop, created to invite prosperity and welcome guests. We will be making beautiful paper and cardstock Rangoli circles to decorate your home and celebrate this Festival of Lights. Supplies are limited. events.title: Sci-Fi & Fantasy Book Club
events.description: Join us to read The Cyberiad by Stanislaw Lem. You can register for the club and get a copy of the book at the adult reference desk. "Trurl and Klapaucius are 'constructors'; they travel around the universe creating machines of astonishing inventiveness and power and visiting a bewildering variety of violent, peculiar and morose civilizations. The Cyberiad is oddly reminiscent of Gulliver's Travels, The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, The Phantom Tollbooth and Alice in Wonderland. Charming, mind-bending and anarchic, it is perhaps Lem's greatest work. This edition includes all of Daniel Mroz's hallucinatory original illustrations." events.title: Music & Movement Storytime

events.title: TeenHQ MakerSpace Studio
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Middle and high schoolers: Come explore the TeenHQ Maker Space! Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, Glow Forge, Sewing & Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies. Work with our teen librarian to bring your idea to life. Each machine and other materials have limitations and time requirements. Pre-registration is recommended to reserve your spot. If registered participants have not arrived by 4:30 PM, their spots will be given to those waiting. All services are provided for free to middle and high school students (grades 6-12). Younger people and adults are not permitted in the area unless required to assist with a disability. Pre-registration will start 1 week before the start of the program. Please un-register yourself if you find you're unable to attend at a later date. Registration closes 1 hour before the start of the program. There will not be a waitlist for pre-registration. Drop-ins will be accepted if not all registration slots are filled and if not all registered individuals arrive by 4:30 PM. The area is wheelchair accessible from the Children's Room elevator. Other accommodations can be made available upon request. Please note that each device requires time to set up, use, and complete whatever task you're wanting to use the space for. Be sure that you have enough time in your schedule to attend the program. Not all tasks may be completed before the end of the program and you may need to return to get your completed items or pause your task and restart at another studio session. We appreciate your patience and flexibility. 3D Printing: All requested prints must take less than 4.5 hours to print. All requested prints will need to be picked up at a later date. Contact information is required for notification of pick-up. 3D print quality and the time needed to complete prints are not guaranteed. Multiple objects can be printed as long as the total time does not exceed 4.5 hours. Poster Printing: All prints must be assembled on a 2"x3" canvas and printed as a PNG file. Please see the regularly scheduled poster printing event for further details. One poster per teen per day. Glow Forge: Create a custom engraved object. Object should follow similar guidelines to the Custom Keychain Program. Complexity of request is at the discretion of the librarian. Sewing & Serger Machines: It is recommended that you bring your own fabric and thread if fabric is special or color is a factor. Scrap material and thread are available, but we cannot guarantee material quality or availability. An iron and ironing board are also available. Cricut: Basic Cricut supplies are available, such as construction and cardstock paper. If your project is specialized, such as requiring iron-on, you'll need to bring your own materials. It is recommended that you know the requirements for any materials you provide. Button Press: TeenHQ offers two sizes of button presses. We cannot offer printing. If you bring your own printout of buttons, it must be printed on standard printer paper. Paper thicker than standard printer paper cannot be used on the button presses. All measurements below are diameters in inches. Small Button Press: 1.25"; Large Button Press: 2.25"; Picture Size: 1.156"; Cut Line: 1.629"; Picture Size: 2.063"; Cut Line: 2.625".
events.blurb: Make projects in the TeenHQ Maker Space, with 3D printers, a Glowforge, sewing machines, a Cricut and a button press for middle and high schoolers.

events.title: Hindi for Everyday Life
events.description: This is an interactive, structured program designed for children ages 5-12 who would like to learn Hindi. It is perfectly tailored for learners from all backgrounds, whether they hear Hindi at home or are exploring it for the very first time. The curriculum nurtures the four core language skills—speaking, listening, reading, and writing—in alignment with US Academic Standards and the California World Languages Framework. Children will learn through physical workbooks, worksheets and short audio/visual tools provided for the program, ensuring a rich and engaging experience. events.title: 3D Printing One-on-One Appointment
events.description: Need help with 3D printing or looking for guided, hands-on experience? This session is ideal for beginners seeking practical experience, guided support, and confidence in using 3D printing technology. This is also a good opportunity for those who attended our 3D Design & Printing workshop and now want to try their hands at it. Participants will have the opportunity to print a simple model under supervision. If you do not have a design, you may choose a free design from Thingiverse or a similar site. All designs are printed in a single color of PLA - filament color at the discretion of the program lead. Designs must print in 1 hour 45 minutes - if you're not sure how long your design will take to print, email cz.sjpl@sjlibrary.org. SJPL reserves the right to refuse any print request. All designs must be compatible with the Creality K1C printer and have a print time of under 45 minutes. Final approval of printability will be determined by the program lead. One appointment per month per person.

events.title: Peter Fletcher Classical Guitar Concert
events.description: Please join us for a performance by classical guitarist Peter Fletcher, with a program titled "Music of Four Centuries." With a rich history of performances spanning prestigious venues across the United States, Fletcher's captivating music resonates with audiences worldwide. He has been invited to perform at esteemed cultural venues across the US, including Carnegie Hall! Peter will perform music from the new CD, as well as the Bach Chaconne, Usher Waltz by Russian composer Nikita Koshkin, a very special arrangement of the famous Shaker hymn Simple Gifts, and music by Giuliani, Ponce and Tansman. The concert will culminate with the luscious Cordoba and powerful Leyenda by Spanish composer Isaac Albeniz. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

events.title: First Thursday Robotics with Bellarmine FTC
events.description: Join us for a monthly interactive robotics demonstration presented by First Tech Challenge (FTC) Team 23222 from Bellarmine College Preparatory School. Watch these high-tech devices perform a variety of tasks, or take a controller and try maneuvering one yourself! You'll learn about all aspects of robots, from the parts that affect their capabilities to the programs that direct their behavior. This program is intended for children ages 5 and up. Adult supervision is required. Free: No registration required.
events.blurb: Watch Bellarmine's FTC robotics team demo their robots and take a controller to try maneuvering one yourself.

events.title: Celebrate Diwali: Traditional Stories, Music and Dance
events.description: Come join us to celebrate the Festival of Lights—Diwali! Immerse your family in an interactive Indian classical dance and storytelling program that brings the traditions, stories and spirit of Diwali to life through movement, music and audience participation. Diwali tales brought to life through expressive Indian classical movement, music and rhythms and concludes with a joyful group dance! This vibrant event welcomes families experiencing Indian dance and Diwali for the first time while offering South Asian families a wonderful opportunity to see their heritage represented and celebrated in their local library. Open to all backgrounds, this colorful, musical program guarantees fun for everyone whether you are deeply familiar with Indian culture or discovering it for the very first time! This program is generously sponsored by the SJPL Foundation's Pat Dando Endowment Fund and the Friends of the Almaden Branch Library.
events.blurb: Watch an Indian classical dance and storytelling program for Diwali, with music and audience participation, at Almaden Library.

events.title: Digital Skills: Internet Safety and Security
events.description: Learn to keep your personal information safe and secure with easy-to-follow lessons from our dedicated tech mentor! You'll learn about program features that protect your data, as well as how to recognize common online scams. With SJPL's Digital Skill Building Pathways, you can practice the skills essential to living and working in the digital world. Learning paths include free lessons, resources, and library events like computer classes. Practice your digital skills at your own pace at sjpl.org/digital-skills or find a program at your local San José Public Library location. Free. Pre-registration is not required. #digitalskillbuildingpathways #dsb Digital Skills
events.blurb: Learn how to protect your personal information and recognize common online scams from a tech mentor at Rose Garden Library.

events.title: Reading Buddies

events.title: Lucha Libro
events.description: Lucha Libro is a family-friendly, high-energy public library program that combines children's story time with live, Mexican-style lucha libre masked wrestling. Founded in 2024 by Jerry Rocha and Victor Dwight, the initiative turns libraries into wrestling rings to promote youth literacy and make reading exciting. Free. No registration is required. Limited space available. Lucha Libro es un programa de la biblioteca pública, dinámico y apto para toda la familia, que combina la hora del cuento para niños con combates de lucha libre mexicana —con luchadores enmascarados— en vivo. Gratis. No es necesario registrarse. Espacio limitado.

events.title: Social Workers in the Library Drop-In Hours
events.description: Advice | Information | Referral. Social Workers in the Library offers free social service information and referrals*. Our staff can meet with you, approach your needs without judgement, and help you find where to go for shelter, food, showers, mental health services, legal help, and more. Free. No registration required. *Disclaimer: SJPL's Social Work in the Library does not establish a social worker-client relationship. SJPL does not offer case management or extensive follow-up services. We will try our best to get you connected to any resource we know of that could suit your needs. Tư Vấn / Thông Tin / Giới Thiệu Nhân Viên Xã Hội trong Thư Viện cung cấp miễn phí thông tin về những dịch vụ xã hội và giới thiệu. Nhân viên của chúng tôi có thể gặp gỡ bạn, tiếp cận với nhu cầu của bạn mà không đánh giá, và giúp bạn tìm những nơi để đến trú ẩn, thực phẩm, tắm rửa, những dịch vụ sức khoẻ tâm thần, trợ giúp pháp lý, và nhiều hơn nữa. Miễn phí. Không bắt buộc phải đăng ký. Từ chối trách nhiệm: Nhân Viên Xã Hội của SJPL trong Thư Viện không thiết lập mối quan hệ giữa một nhân viên xã hội và khách hàng. SJPL không cung cấp quản lý các trường hợp hoặc dịch vụ theo dõi mở rộng. Chúng tôi sẽ cố gắng hết sức để kết nối bạn với bất kỳ nguồn nào chúng tôi biết có thể phù hợp với nhu cầu của bạn. Asesoramiento | Información | Referencia. Este programa ofrece información y referencias de servicios sociales gratuitos. Nuestro personal puede reunirse con usted, abordar sus necesidades sin juicio y ayudarle a encontrar dónde ir para obtener refugio, comida, duchas, servicios de salud mental, ayuda legal y más. Gratis. No se requiere registro. *Aviso: El Trabajo Social en la Biblioteca de SJPL no establece una relación de Trabajador Social-Cliente. SJPL no ofrece gestión de casos ni servicios de seguimiento extensos. Haremos todo lo posible por conectarte con cualquier recurso que conozcamos y que pueda satisfacer tus necesidades.

events.title: ELL Beginning English: The Basics

The ELL Beginning English program meets weekly at the library in the library's Community Room with a trained facilitator. Free. No Registration required. Vineland's English Learning series: ELL Beginning English: The Basics - A beginner program for learners with limited English skills; approximately levels 0-2; ELL Intermediate English: Grammar and Vocabulary Club - An intermediate program for learners that know some English but want to learn more complex English; approximately levels 2-3; ELL Advanced English: Conversation Club - An advanced program for learners to practice speaking and listening while also learning about American culture and idioms; approximately levels 3-4; ELL Writing Club: A program where high beginners to advanced level English language learners can learn and practice their English writing skills; approximately levels 2-4; ELL Reading & Speaking: A program where high beginners to advanced level English language learners can read aloud and practice their pronunciation; approximately levels 2-4.

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Spies Among Us
events.description: This is a rare look into the inner workings of a data-driven surveillance state run by one of the most feared secret police forces the world has ever known – East Germany's Stasi. A personal investigation into family secrets by Peter Keup, a Stasi victim-turned-historian, takes a turn when he contacts the men who ran the system. These are the first dialogues between Stasi officers and a victim ever recorded. Through these encounters a terrifying mosaic is built of the lengths people go to maintain power in a dictatorship, as well as the indomitable human spirit that seeks truth and self-determination. Jamie Coughlin Silverman and Gabriel Silverman are award-winning journalists-turned-documentary filmmakers. Their first feature documentary, TransMilitary, won the Audience Award for Best Documentary at SXSW and received critical acclaim. TransMilitary was represented by Cinetic Media and distributed by Gravitas Ventures. It premiered on Logo TV and Amazon Prime. The film screened at more than 100 film festivals worldwide, and the Silvermans were named to the 2018 Top 10 Filmmakers to Watch list by The Independent. The Silvermans are Gotham (IFP) Documentary Lab Fellows and CNN/Film Independent Episodic Lab Fellows. Their work has been supported by the International Documentary Association, Catapult Film Fund, Jonathan Logan Family Foundation, and Frameline Completion Fund. They are the first recipients of funding from the GLAAD Media Institute. Their production company, SideXSide Studios, is a global documentary firm that specializes in consequential and high-visibility non-fiction storytelling. Prior to SideXSide Studios, the Silvermans worked in leading newsrooms. Gabe was a video journalist at The Washington Post where his work was recognized with more than a dozen awards, including an Edward R. Murrow Award for his investigative work, a White House News Photographers Award for Best Documentary, and two Emmy nominations. Jamie was the supervising producer for USA Today Sports, where she led editorial and branded video content strategy. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.

events.title: Adult Nonfiction Book Discussion: Nothing to Envy: Ordinary Lives in North Korea
events.description: In November, the Adult Nonfiction Book Group will discuss Nothing to Envy: Ordinary Lives in North Korea by Barbara Demick (2009). The book is based on Demick's interviews over a seven-year period with six North Koreans who escaped the country and the regime. The vast majority of North Koreans know little more of the world beyond their borders than the rest of the world knows about their daily lives under the Kim Jong-il regime. Without easy access to healthcare and with frequent food shortages, life for the average working family in North Korea under Kim Jong-Il's rule is and was grim by Western standards. As of the publication date of this book, ordinary citizens have few if any civil rights and almost no recourse to protest injustice, as complaints and almost any sign of dissatisfaction with the regime could lead to imprisonment. The Adult Nonfiction Book Group meets on the second Sunday of each month at 11 am in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Backman - January; The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February; South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March; Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April; The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May; The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June; Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July; Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August; The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September; We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October; What We Can Know by Ian McEwan - November; The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/

events.title: Documentaries: Holodomor Remembrance Day
events.description: The Holodomor, the famine that killed millions of Ukrainians in the 1930s, was not widely known or acknowledged until the fall of the Soviet Union in the 1990s. Established in 1998, Holodomor Remembrance Day is observed on the fourth Saturday of November to remember those who died during the Holodomor. Join us for Palo Alto City Library's second annual program commemorating this event and its lasting effects for some in our community today. Three short documentaries will give us the historical background that reverberates in current events. Descriptions of the documentaries below were written by their creators. Holodomor: How Millions of Ukrainians Died of Starvation During Stalin-Era Mass Famine (Radio Free Europe, 2019, two minutes). Each year, on the fourth Saturday of November, Ukraine remembers the millions who died during the Holodomor, the Stalin-era famine that devastated the population in 1932-1933. Many countries consider it to have been genocide. Minnesota Memories of the Holodomor (PBS, 2025, 26 minutes). In an extraordinary exploration of the transmission of traumatic memory within families, communities and across generations, Ukrainians in Minneapolis-St. Paul share their family stories about the Holodomor artificial famine of 1932-33 and the local community's efforts to come to terms with genocide, even as war once again threatens the existence of Ukrainians as a people. Holodomor: Voices of Survivors (2015, 30 minutes). Twenty-five Ukrainian Canadians tell their stories of survival during the Holodomor--death inflicted by starvation--a genocide of Ukrainian people engineered by Joseph Stalin during 1932 and 1933. Through compelling eyewitness accounts, the film brings into focus a pivotal and little-known period in history, the consequences of which continue to reverberate today. Books on this reading list will be on display and available. Registration is not necessary, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.
events.blurb: Watch a documentary at Rinconada Library on the Holodomor, the 1930s famine that killed millions of Ukrainians.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 15th: Topic: An Epicurean in Public Life: Justice and Injustice "Justice's greatest reward is peace of mind." Fragment 80. "Justice was never an entity in itself. It is a kind of agreement not to harm or be harmed, made when men associate with each other at any time and in communities of any size whatsoever." Principal Doctrine 33. "Injustice is not an evil in itself. Its evil lies in the anxious fear that you will not elude those who have authority to punish such misdeeds." Principal Doctrine 34. "It is impossible to leave the pleasant life without also living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely it is impossible to live sensibly, nobly, and justly without living pleasantly. A person who does not have a pleasant life is not living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely the person who does not have these virtues cannot live pleasantly." Principal Doctrine 5. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 8 (pp. 80-91). Some Questions to Discuss: Based on the ideas expressed in the Principal Doctrines, what is Epicurus's view on the source of justice in society? What is the connection that Epicurus draws between injustice and corrosive desires according to Austin's analysis of his views on injustice? Is it easy to be just? Is it hard to be unjust?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

(There is actually a correct answer!) What are chill hours and how many are good? Semi-dwarf? True dwarf? Multi-graft? How do I plant a new tree? Local nurseries will begin stocking bare root fruit trees in December. Come learn what decisions affect the success of your orchard. Don Bollinger leads the orchard team at the Master Gardener demonstration garden at Martial Cottle Park in South San Jose. He leads year-round hands-on learning and demonstrations of fruit tree management including winter pruning, water, fertilizer, pest management, soil health and fruit variety selection. No need to register, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.

events.title: Medicare: Enrollment, 2027 Updates and Plan Review Tips
events.description: The Medicare Annual Enrollment Period (AEP) runs from October 15 through December 7 each year. During this time, Medicare beneficiaries can review and make changes to their Medicare health and prescription drug coverage for the coming year. Join HICAP (Health Insurance Counseling & Advocacy Program) for a free educational presentation covering Medicare updates taking effect in 2027, Medicare Advantage and Part D plan review strategies, and important factors to consider when evaluating your coverage options. Learn how to compare plan costs, provider networks, prescription drug coverage, and other benefits to determine whether your current plan continues to meet your needs. Following the presentation, HICAP counselors will be available for free one-on-one counseling sessions to answer Medicare questions and help attendees review their coverage options. HICAP counselors are unbiased and are not affiliated with any insurance company. The one-on-one sessions will be on a first-come, first-served basis. HICAP is a program of Sourcewise providing free Medicare counseling to Santa Clara County residents. Who Should Attend? Current Medicare beneficiaries reviewing their coverage for 2027; Individuals approaching Medicare eligibility; Family members and caregivers assisting a Medicare beneficiary. What You Will Learn: Medicare updates taking effect in 2027; How the Annual Enrollment Period works; Medicare Advantage and Part D plan review tips; How to compare costs, coverage, and provider networks; Prescription drug coverage considerations; When it may make sense to change plans; Resources and assistance available through HICAP. What to Bring: A complete list of your prescription medications, including dosage and quantity, for accurate plan comparisons. Your Medicare card (optional, but helpful). HICAP counselors will have laptops available for Medicare plan reviews, but attendees are welcome to bring their own laptop or tablet. Time Required: The time needed to complete a plan comparison varies depending on the number of prescriptions and coverage options being reviewed. Most plan reviews take approximately 30–60 minutes. This program is intended for Santa Clara County residents. Please register if you would like to receive a reminder about the presentation. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org. About Sourcewise: Since 1973, Sourcewise has provided services and support to seniors in Santa Clara County. Sourcewise aims to inform, educate, and prepare all adults within Santa Clara County to better navigate their health and life options.

events.title: Adult Book Discussion: Theft
events.description: In November, the Cupertino Library Adult Book Discussion Group will talk about the 2025 novel Theft by Nobel Prize-winning author Abdulrazak Gurnah. Karim and Badar are two young men living on the East African island of Zanzibar. Karim's mother Raya leaves her abusive older husband when Karim is three, taking her son with her. However, when she finds a happy marriage with her new husband Haji Othman, Raya allows her parents to raise her son instead. Years later, when Karim is a university student living with his mother and stepfather for convenience, he meets and befriends the orphaned teenaged boy Badar, whose neglectful relatives force him to become a domestic servant in Haji Othmann's household. There, Badar is treated as a servant, although he is actually Othman's nephew. Fauzia, Karim's beautiful, studious girlfriend, teaches Badar the cooking and housekeeping skills he needs to become a successful domestic servant. Badar's fragile new security is abruptly destroyed when he is accused of theft and dismissed. Even though Karim helps him get a new job at a local hotel, things are never the same between them. Meetings are held in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

events.title: Don't Get Scammed This Holiday Season
events.description: Online holiday shopping is convenient, but scammers are counting on you to be busy, rushed, and hunting for a good deal. As more of us turn to online shopping and charitable giving this time of year, fraudsters are getting better at looking legitimate. How can you tell if that website is a real store? Is that unbelievable social media deal actually a bargain, or a trap? And when you donate to a cause, how do you know your gift is going where you intended? Join us for a practical presentation that will help you shop and give with confidence. You'll learn how to: Verify that an online store is legitimate before you enter your credit card number; Read and understand product reviews, including how to spot fake or paid reviews; Recognize counterfeit and nonexistent products advertised on social media; Identify charity scams and make sure your donations reach the people and organizations you want to help. You'll leave with simple tips and a few trusted resources to help you stay safe shopping for the holidays and beyond. Keep them on hand all season long. Whether you're a seasoned online shopper or just getting started, this program will help you protect your money, your personal information, and your holiday spirit. Bring your questions and your own stories. Your experience might help a neighbor avoid a scam too! Registration is recommended but NOT required. Register in order to receive a reminder email the day before the event.
events.blurb: Learn how to spot holiday shopping scams and protect yourself online at Rinconada Library on Wednesday morning.

events.title: Author Event with Dr. Carol Peyser
events.description: Please join us to hear Dr. Carol Peyser discuss her book, A Hidden Fate (She Writes Press, October 27, 2026), a literary novel interweaving multiple themes: the emotional consequences of genetic foreknowledge, the weight of family secrets and deceptions, overcoming childhood trauma, and the unexpected conflicts of vision and conviction that can emerge in love relationships. The novel has received a starred Kirkus review, and a Book Life reviewer described it as "great for fans of Lisa Genova's Inside the O'Briens and Abraham Verghese's The Covenant of Water." Early in her career, she directed the Huntington's Disease Clinic at Johns Hopkins Hospital right when predictive testing became available to people at risk for the terrible disease. Dr. Peyser saw first-hand how genetic knowledge — and even the possibility of obtaining it — alters a person's relationship to their future and to their family. Interacting with people deciding what they wanted, or might not want, to know about their future seared these issues into her heart. Later, as a geriatric psychiatrist on the Stanford faculty and in private practice in Menlo Park, she saw these questions multiply. Descendants of those with Alzheimer's disease, major depression, and other heritable illnesses grappled with fears about genetic risk — and with the weight of what to keep private, and what to disclose — to whom, and when. These questions of genetic knowledge, secrecy, and their consequences are at the heart of the book. How does wondering what might be coded in our DNA impact us? How does knowing what lies in our genes change us? How are families impacted by the new possibilities genomic testing raises?
events.blurb: Hear author Dr. Carol Peyser speak at an evening author event at Rinconada Library.

events.title: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1: Drawing with Time and Rhythm
events.description: In this one-hour figure-drawing workshop, participants will draw together with pencils for 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute—and sometimes even 30 seconds. We will begin with longer drawing times and slowly move to shorter, faster ones. Participants can try different pencil pressure, movement, and speed as the timing changes. Participants may volunteer to pose for the group. As we draw, we will watch different poses and body movements and follow the changing rhythm together. The timing will be repeated about three times. Participants will make several drawings on 11 × 14-inch paper and one larger drawing on 18 × 24-inch paper, arranging several figures on one sheet. The workshop is open to adults of all levels. No drawing experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including 4B pencils, five sheets of 11 × 14-inch paper, and one sheet of 18 × 24-inch paper for each participant. Duration: 60 minutes.
events.blurb: Draw with pencils in timed rounds of 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute, in a one-hour figure-drawing workshop.

events.title: Tai Chi with Nelson Ng
events.description: Join us for Tai Chi sessions with Nelson Ng! In this weekly class, participants will learn the basic principles and the philosophy behind Tai Chi, gaining flexibility and a better sense of balance through slow, gentle movement. Nelson started learning Chen's Tai Chi in 1989 from Master Gene Chen, who was a disciple of Grandmaster Feng Zhi Qiang. Nelson has been teaching since 2014. This class is free and open to beginners as well as those who have previous Tai Chi experience. People of all ages are welcome. You must sign in upon arrival.
events.blurb: Learn Tai Chi principles and practice slow, gentle movements with instructor Nelson Ng to build balance and flexibility.

events.title: Korean Calligraphy Workshop: Writing Your Name in Hangul with Flow and Rhythm
events.description: In this 90-minute workshop, participants will use calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper to write their names in Hangul. Because Hangul is based on sound, names from many different languages can be written in Hangul according to how they are pronounced. Participants will see how their names look in Hangul and experience the rhythm of Korean writing through brush movement and repetition. Participants can get help writing their names in Hangul along the way. We will begin with simple brush exercises on hanji paper. Participants will practice moving the whole arm, changing the pressure and speed of the brush, and making different kinds of lines. They will then write their names several times, following the movement and rhythm of each brushstroke. At the end of the workshop, participants will write their names on a hanji fan. No previous calligraphy or Korean language experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including calligraphy brushes, ink, hanji paper, and one hanji fan for each participant. Duration: 90 minutes.
events.blurb: Write your name in Hangul using calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper in a 90-minute workshop.
