events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Panama Deception
events.description: A riveting Academy Award-winning critique of the government's history of militarization, made all the more timely by the current war on terrorism. 1993 Academy Award, Best Documentary Feature. Read the Acceptance Speech by Barbara Trent. The Panama Deception documents the untold story of the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama; the events which led to it; the excessive force used; the enormity of the death and destruction; and the devastating aftermath. The Panama Deception uncovers the real reasons for this internationally condemned attack, presenting a view of the invasion which widely differs from that portrayed by the U.S. media and exposes how the U.S. government and the mainstream media suppressed information about this foreign policy disaster. The Panama Deception includes never before seen footage of the invasion and its aftermath, as well as interviews with both invasion proponents like Gen. Maxwell Thurman, Panamanian President Endara and Pentagon spokesperson Pete Williams, and opponents like U.S. Representative Charles Rangel (D-NY), Panamanian human rights workers Olga Mejia and Isabel Corro and former Panamanian diplomat Humberto Brown. Network news clips and media critics contribute to a staggering analysis of media control and self-censorship relevant to any news coverage today, particularly during times of war. Among the film's excellent reviews are: "meticulously researched" (Hal Hinson, Washington Post); "outstanding" (Betsy Sherman, Boston Globe); "tough.... provocative.... moving.... beautifully edited" (Vincent Canby, New York Times); and "lays out simply and forcefully the case against the 'official' version" (Peter Rainer, Los Angeles Times). The Empowerment Project (EP) worked on this production for two years. EP first came to prominence in 1988 with the release of the equally acclaimed Coverup: Behind the Iran Contra Affair. EP is a non-profit media resource center committed to democratizing the media. Each year, hundreds of independent filmmakers use EP's edit facilities and other services. Since its August 1992 release, The Panama Deception has played in 80 cities, including an eight-week run in Seattle and a five-week holdover in New York City. The film appeared in video stores in August 1993. It was cablecast on Cinemax in the United States during October of that same year. Many local affiliates of PBS have broadcast the film, but national PBS has refused to broadcast the film despite the Congressional mandate explicitly requiring that both sides of controversial issues be included in PBS's overall programming. Internationally, the film has been broadcast in Australia, Canada, Poland, Hong Kong, France, Spain, Portugal, the U.K., Iran, Israel, Finland, Switzerland, Mexico, Argentina, Japan, Norway, the People's Republic of China, S. Korea, Italy, Turkey, Russia, S. Africa, the Netherlands, the Philippines, Algeria, Malaysia, and Czechoslovakia. A ban on the film originally imposed by the Panamanian government was lifted in March 1993, following strong internal and international pressure. Funding for The Panama Deception has been provided, in part, by: Channel Four in London, Rhino Home Video, the I. Roderick MacArthur Foundation, the Rex Foundation, the Peace Development Fund, the National Council of Churches, the Car Eth Foundation, the Vietnam Veterans of America Foundation, the Funding Exchange/Paul Robeson Fund for Film and Video, The Charles Lawrence Keith and Clara Miller Foundation, Essential Information, the Vanguard Public Foundation, Lucille Banta, Michelle Connor, filmmaker Michael Moore and hundreds of individual donors. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch the Academy Award-winning documentary on Panama and discuss its themes of militarization.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 6th: Topic: Epicurus's Challenge to Our Society: Raising a Tranquil Child "The wise man will marry and beget children, as Epicurus tells us in Problems and his work On Nature; but he will marry according to his station in life, whatever it may be." Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, 10:119. "Natural wealth is limited and easily obtained; the riches of idle fancies go on forever." Principal Doctrine 15. "Some men spend their whole life furnishing for themselves the things proper to life without realizing that at our birth each of us was poured a moral brew to drink." Vatican Sayings 30. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 17 (pp. 180-190). Some Questions to Discuss: In our society, how realistic is Emily Austin's Epicurean plan for raising a child? What are possible impediments to the realization of her plan? What are possible solutions for overcoming these obstacles?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join the Graphic Novel Book Club at Mitchell Park Library to discuss the group's latest pick, Thursday evenings.

events.title: Pageturners: The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon
events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Backman - January; The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February; South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March; Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April; The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May; The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June; Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July; Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August; The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September; We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October; What We Can Know by Ian McEwan - November; The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
events.blurb: Discuss Michael Chabon's The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay with fellow readers at the Pageturners book group.

Come discover their natural behaviors, their big personalities, and what makes them such cool animals. Coloring pages will be available for the attendees. Registration required. As founder of Clorofil, an animal advocacy nonprofit and micro-sanctuary, Isabelle rescues chickens and gives them a safe home where they can just be chickens. Learn more about them at www.clorofil.org. Project Humane Kind teaches compassion and respect for living beings. Through humane education, they combat cruelty and indifference and bring awareness to the intelligent, social, and emotional depths of our fellow animals. Visit them online at www.projecthumanekind.org.

events.title: Celebrating Yalda Night
events.description: Join us for a special Yalda Night celebration with children's author Anahita Tamaddon and a reading of her book, Yalda Night! Experience the beauty of this cherished Persian tradition through a Yalda-inspired story, music, and a fun paper craft featuring one of Yalda's beloved symbols. Yalda, the longest night of the year, is a joyful celebration of family, storytelling, and togetherness as we welcome the arrival of winter. All craft materials will be provided. Children ages three and up, along with their adult caregivers, are invited to participate. Materials will be available while supplies last. While registration isn't required and doesn't guarantee a spot, it is recommended if you'd like a reminder about the event. برای جشن ویژه‌ی شب یلدا همراه با نویسنده‌ی کتاب‌های کودک، آناهیتا تمدن، به ما بپیوندید. در این برنامه با زیبایی‌های این سنت دیرینه‌ی ایرانی از طریق قصه‌ای با حال‌وهوای یلدا، موسیقی و ساخت کاردستی کاغذی با الهام از یکی از نمادهای دوست‌داشتنی یلدا آشنا خواهیم شد. شب یلدا، بلندترین شب سال، فرصتی برای جشن گرفتن در کنار خانواده و عزیزان، قصه‌گویی و با هم بودن و همچنین خوشامدگویی به فصل زمستان است. تمام وسایل مورد نیاز برای ساخت کاردستی فراهم خواهد بود.
events.blurb: Hear author Anahita Tamaddon read her book Yalda Night and make a Yalda-inspired paper craft.

events.title: Mindfulness Meditation
events.description: Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. It is open to all levels of experience, and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. You can learn more about Phuong here and can watch her meditation videos on the library's YouTube channel here.
events.blurb: Sit for guided sitting and releasing meditation with Phuong Pham, then join a group sharing and Q&A session.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 20th: Topic: Becoming an Epicurean? "In other occupations, the reward comes with difficulty after their completion, but in philosophy delight coincides with knowledge. For enjoyment does not come after learning, but learning and enjoyment come together." Vatican Sayings 27. "We must not pretend to be philosophers, but be philosophers in truth. For we do not stand in need of the appearance of health but of true health." Vatican Sayings 54. "By love of true philosophy we are delivered from every disturbing and painful desire." Fragment 66. "The most important consequence of self-sufficiency is freedom." Vatican Sayings 77. "The impassive soul disturbs neither itself nor others." Vatican Sayings 79. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 23 (pp. 241-251) and 24 (pp. 252-266). Some Questions to Discuss: In your opinion, which of Epicurus's ideas, if any, have not lost their currency and would be beneficial to our society? What needs to be done to implement them? What challenges may their implementation face?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: NeuroSphere: Neuroscience and More!
events.description: Come join the teen-led group NeuroSphere! This session will dive into the basics of brain function, fun activities to test your brainpower, and an introduction to future career opportunities. There will be snacks; feel free to bring a friend! We're a group of high school students driven by a passion for neuroscience and the wonders of the brain. Our mission is to inspire curiosity and spark a love for science in younger students by creating engaging, hands-on learning experiences. Through NeuroSphere, we hope to share our knowledge, connect with the community, and encourage the next generation of future scientists and innovators! Questions? Email neurosphereyouth@gmail.com.
events.blurb: Join teen-led NeuroSphere to dig into brain function basics and test your brainpower with hands-on activities.
events.attendanceNote: The library's title lists grades 3–8, but its description says grades 2–7 only. Confirm eligibility with Mitchell Park Library.

events.title: Tai Chi with Nelson Ng
events.description: Join us for Tai Chi sessions with Nelson Ng! In this weekly class, participants will learn the basic principles and the philosophy behind Tai Chi, gaining flexibility and a better sense of balance through slow, gentle movement. Nelson started learning Chen's Tai Chi in 1989 from Master Gene Chen, who was a disciple of Grandmaster Feng Zhi Qiang. Nelson has been teaching since 2014. This class is free and open to beginners as well as those who have previous Tai Chi experience. People of all ages are welcome. You must sign in upon arrival.
events.blurb: Learn Tai Chi principles and practice slow, gentle movements with instructor Nelson Ng to build balance and flexibility.

events.description: Join us for a monthly meetup designed for intermediate and advanced photographers hosted by Matthew Tw Huang. Whether you're into portrait, landscape, or any other type of photography, all are welcome! Each session will feature discussions on techniques, tips for improving your craft, and other aspects of photography. Ideas for 5-10 min topics, photo stories, or presentations can be emailed to matthewtwhuang@gmail.com. There will be time for a couple of ideas to be presented at each meeting. The format will evolve based on your interests and feedback, creating a supportive and dynamic space for photographers to connect, learn, and grow.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join the Graphic Novel Book Club at Mitchell Park Library to discuss the group's latest pick, Thursday evenings.

events.title: Pageturners: Double Play on the Red Line with Raj Oza
events.description: Join us for a special discussion with local author Raj Oza about his book Double Play on the Red Line. Here's a chance to talk to a writer about his writing process and to hear how he came to write this novel. Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
events.blurb: Talk with local author Raj Oza about Double Play on the Red Line and hear how he came to write the novel.

events.title: Open Sewing Studio
events.description: Do you have a sewing project but need the equipment and space? Are you interested in learning about the basics of a sewing machine? Open Sewing Studio is a space for both beginners looking to learn as well as experienced sewists looking for the time and space to work on their project. We will have sewing machines, table space, fabric scraps, and tools available for attendees. Bring your own projects and have fun! Note: Teens and adults only. Use of machines will be on a first-come, first-served basis due to limited supply. Our staff is only available to support very basic projects. Please keep in mind Open Sewing Studio is limited to 1.5 hours.

events.title: Music & Movement
events.description: Join us for a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning for all ages. Join us in celebrating Día de los Muertos with Felicia and Gustavo, who will be presenting a craft where participants can create their own Day of the Dead altar and try some culturally relevant foods related to the celebration! Thank you to Felicia and Gustavo, who have offered their time and hard work to make this a very festive occasion for the little ones! Free! First-come, first-served during the event.

events.title: Reading to Furry Friends
events.description: Tell a story to a Furry Friend! Children are invited to practice reading to gentle, trained assistance dogs who love books! Practice reading skills while relaxing next to a cute Furry Friend. Eliminate fines/fees related to lost or damaged items by being read to. Attend this program to have $5 deducted from juvenile accounts for every 15 minutes you are read to. Please check in at the 2nd Floor Info Desk for additional information. For youth ages 0-10. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Practice reading skills aloud to gentle, trained assistance dogs at the library.

events.title: Mahjong Club
events.description: Play Hong Kong style Mahjong at the library! Seasoned players and beginners are welcome. Learn the basics or refresh your knowledge of the game. You'll learn: how to start the game; what the tiles mean; the rules of the game and how to win; and how to create sets and play. Playing Mahjong improves cognitive function, helps reduce stress, and creates a sense of community. This program is suitable for adults and seniors. Free. Registration required. Drop-ins welcome depending on space.
events.blurb: Learn Hong Kong style Mahjong, from what the tiles mean to how to build sets and win, whether beginner or seasoned.

events.title: Interview & Networking Skills Workshop
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose

Thank you to the Friends of the Palo Alto Library (FOPAL) for their generous support.

events.title: Ukraine: Culture, Geography, History and Heritage
events.description: Nora Mason, a native-born Ukrainian and long-time Saratoga resident, will present a program on the culture of Ukraine and how its geography has contributed to tragic invasions over time. She will share her family's WWII story and how they ultimately immigrated to the United States. She will also touch on inspiring efforts to help the people of Ukraine today. Program co-sponsored by the Los Gatos-Saratoga AAUW.
events.blurb: Hear Ukrainian-born Saratoga resident Nora Mason talk about Ukraine's culture and how its geography has shaped its history of invasions.

events.title: Weekly Citizenship Class

events.description: Do you enjoy working with knitting, crocheting, or tatting? Everyone 7 and up is invited to participate, and younger children are welcome to accompany their families.

events.description: Learn key concepts in coding through origami, the art of folding paper. Participants will fold a different animal or object each month. No registration required.

events.title: Family Craft: Pom Pom Photo Frames
events.description: Create and decorate a pom pom photo frame! Children ages 4–11 are invited to make a unique design using popsicle sticks, glue, sequins, buttons, and pom poms. events.blurb: Decorate a pom pom photo frame with your child using popsicle sticks and sequins at the Children's Library.

events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Groups larger than 10, please contact us before joining as space and seating are limited.

events.title: Insiders: Activities
events.description: Join us for socializing, finding new friends, networking, making jokes, learning to play Dungeons & Dragons, and having fun with art! Insiders programs are geared towards teens and adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities. Caregivers are welcome to join. Snacks will be provided. Walk-ins are welcome!
events.blurb: Hang out, make art, and try Dungeons & Dragons at this social meetup for teens and adults.

events.title: Music & Storytelling with Kirk Waller
events.description: Join us for a performance with musician and storyteller Kirk Waller! Kirk mesmerizes audiences of all ages with a dynamic blend of music, movement, and storytelling. Journey with him through captivating tales from long ago and far away, brought vividly to life through his energetic and engaging performance style.
events.blurb: Watch musician and storyteller Kirk Waller mix music, movement, and stories in a performance for audiences of all ages.

events.title: Everyone Can Code: Sphero Battle Robots
events.description: Use Sphero robots to compete in a balloon-popping battle. Team up with students to take down your opponents. Learn the basics of Sphero. Learn to roll, aim, control the LEDs, change heading, and detect collisions. Once you have the basics down, you can practice coding through simple, beginner-friendly activities.
events.blurb: Team up to pilot Sphero robots in a balloon-popping battle while learning basic coding skills.

events.title: Financial Health and Wellness: Optimizing Social Security Benefits
events.description: Join the Library as we welcome financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada of the Heartland Institute of Financial Education back for a workshop series on financial health and wellness! Registration opens two weeks before the event date and is preferred for each individual session to adequately accommodate seating.
events.blurb: Hear financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada explain strategies for optimizing your Social Security benefits.

events.title: Celebrate Native American Heritage Month! Story and Craft
events.description: Join Librarian Jennifer as we celebrate Native American Heritage Month! We'll be sharing Native American folk tales, then crafting traditional clay pinch pots. Please note that while all ages are welcome, this program is designed for children ages 5 and up. Space and supplies are limited; please arrive on time!
events.blurb: Hear Native American folk tales and craft a clay pinch pot at Palo Alto's Children's Library.

events.title: STEM: Lotus Pond Origami Workshop
events.description: Practice geometry, fractions, and sequential reasoning through folding origami lotuses. This program is recommended for patrons aged 6-11. Registration required; if you are registered, please arrive on time. Registrants who are more than 15 minutes late may lose their registered spot to a walk-in participant.

events.title: Tai Chi for Seniors
events.description: Join us at Tully Library every Thursday for an hour of Tai Chi exercises. Tai Chi improves strength, flexibility, aerobic conditioning, and balance. It's been proven to improve cardiovascular fitness, lower blood pressure, prevent falls, and help people who have arthritis. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Move through an hour of Tai Chi exercises built to boost balance, flexibility, and cardiovascular fitness.

events.title: ESL Conversation Club for English Language Learners (ELL)
events.description: Practice and improve your English-speaking skills in a group setting with a volunteer facilitator, discussing a variety of topics. A basic understanding of English is required. The purpose of this group is to help learners practice speaking and build confidence and comfort when communicating in English.
events.blurb: Build confidence speaking English with a volunteer facilitator at Joyce Ellington Library's conversation club.

No registration is required—just drop in and play!
events.blurb: Try out new tabletop games or bring a favorite to share at Calabazas Library's monthly Game Club.

events.title: LEGO Club
events.description: Visit the library every Tuesday for an hour of fun building with LEGO Bricks! Explore your creativity and utilize your engineering skills to build towers, spaceships, forts, and more! This event is recommended for children 5 and older. Small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards for younger children.
events.blurb: Build towers, spaceships, and forts out of LEGO Bricks during an hour of open building time.

events.title: Tea & Toys: Playdate for Children and Their Caregivers
events.description: Parents & caregivers: bring your little ones ages 5 and younger to a playdate at the Library! Kids will discover new toys and activities while adults will have a chance to chat and get acquainted while sipping tea. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Almaden Branch Library.
events.blurb: Let kids ages 5 and younger try new toys and activities while caregivers chat and sip tea at this library playdate.

events.title: Make Your Own Seasonal Soaps
events.description: In this class, local maker Bea Byrne will guide you through designing and mixing your own personalized soaps. Choose the scents and colors you want, mixing and matching to create unique combinations. Each participant will leave with 3 individual soaps and the know-how to make their own at home!
events.blurb: Mix your own seasonal soaps with local maker Bea Byrne, choosing the scents and colors for your combinations.

events.title: Personal Insight Questions (PIQs) Writing Workshop
events.description: Not confident with your personal insight questions for the UC application or not sure where to start? Work one-on-one with an experienced writing instructor who will help you craft and revise your PIQs that avoid common mistakes and showcase the best of who you are to the admissions team.
events.blurb: Work one-on-one with a writing instructor to craft and revise your UC personal insight questions.

events.blurb: Build your own models from the library's LEGO pieces at Tully Library, with children under 5 accompanied by a parent.

events.title: Learn English: Holiday Fun!

events.title: Volunteer in the Historic Orchard with UC Master Gardeners!
events.description: The Historic Orchard is a 3.3-acre site planted in 1994 and located in Guadalupe Gardens just south of Taylor Street, adjacent to the Heritage Rose Garden and River Park trails. In the 1930s and '40s, almost everyone who lived here was engaged in the business of fruit production: growing, picking, packing, canning, selling, or otherwise supporting the industry. Today, with very few orchards remaining, this is a place where adults and children can come to experience a piece of local history. Fruit harvested from the Historic Orchard is donated to Second Harvest of Silicon Valley and local shelters. Help us maintain the River Park's Historic Orchard with activities including tree planting and pruning; disease diagnosis and treatment; sun scald prevention painting; sheet mulching; experimenting with different types of irrigation or ground cover; and grafting for improved pollination. Chaperones are required for those age 15 and younger. School groups or corporate teams must contact the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteer@grpg.org to schedule events. Restrooms are available at the Rotary Play Garden and will require staff assistance. Address for parking: 438 Coleman Ave. Jose, CA 95110; Meeting location: Historic Orchard (refer to the registration form for a map); Time: 9:30 AM - 11:30 AM; Recurring dates: Every Wednesday

events.title: Festival of Lights: A Diwali Celebration
events.description: Join us at the Mitchell Park Community Center as we celebrate Diwali! Enjoy fun activities for all ages: Ongoing from 2-4 PM: Henna with teaching artist Rachel-Anne Palacios (Adobe Room; henna line closes at 3:30 PM!); Rangoli (chalk coloring craft outside in the Courtyard); Crafts (in Adobe Room); All activities available while supplies last! Performance from 2:30-3:30 PM in El Palo Alto Room by Noorani Dance. Rachel-Anne Palacios is an Afro-Chicana Oakland native, multi-cultural arts educator, and self-taught folk artist. She has been teaching art workshops and classes at Bay Area schools and libraries for over a decade and a half and her lessons and projects are inspired by indigenous cultures and traditional art from around the world. Noorani Dance, founded in 2016 by international Kathak artist, Farah Yasmeen Shaikh, exemplifies Farah's unique artistic expression and vision coupled with the classical and innovative influence and style of Farah's Guru, the late Pandit Chitresh Das. "Noorani" means bright or luminous, with a dual meaning of enlightenment. With Kathak dance as their medium, Noorani Dance is committed to enlightening minds and hearts through the arts.
events.blurb: Celebrate Diwali with the community at Mitchell Park Community Center's Festival of Lights.

There will be three rooms with over 70,000 books, CDs, DVDs, puzzles, etc., new & gently used, all sorted, very reasonably priced! Proceeds benefit the Palo Alto libraries. For the safety and comfort of all participants, masks are suggested and room occupancy will be lower than usual. Please visit fopal.org for more information. Saturday Hours: Bargain Room: 9:30 AM – 4 PM; Children's Room: 10 AM – 4 PM; Main Room: 11 AM – 4 PM. Sunday Hours: All Rooms: 1 PM – 4 PM.
events.blurb: Browse three rooms of over 70,000 used books, CDs, DVDs, and puzzles at Cubberley Community Center.

events.title: Line Dancing with Sandy and Kent
events.description: Join Sandy and Kent for a family-friendly line dancing class! Exercise your brain and body and enhance your balance while dancing to a variety of international music. No partner needed and beginners welcome! You are welcome to practice before and after by checking out their special playlist for this class. This class will take place in the Mitchell Park Bowl. (In the event of rain, the class will move to the Midtown Room inside the Mitchell Park Library.) Sandy and Kent have taught line dancing throughout the Bay Area for ten years. Learn more about them on their YouTube channel. Registration is not required. If you register, you will get an email reminder for the program including a link to the class playlist to practice.
events.blurb: Learn line dancing steps with Sandy and Kent to international music; no partner or experience needed.

events.title: Noon Year's Eve Celebration!
events.description: Not planning to stay up until midnight on New Year's Eve with your little ones? Then join us for a "Noon" Year's Eve celebration! We will count down to noon on Thursday, December 31, complete with a "ball and bubble" drop. We'll ring in the new year with crafts, dancing and music, so bring your party hats and noisemakers! Come dressed in party attire if you'd like! *This event will be held in the Adobe Room of the Mitchell Park Community Center.
events.blurb: Count down to noon with your little ones, with a ball and bubble drop, so no one has to stay up until midnight.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: Bird ID and Guided Hike
events.description: The Park Rangers invite you to learn about the birds living in our riparian habitat and how to ID them! Walk the trails to see the environment they live in and maybe catch a glimpse of a Red-Shouldered Hawk, Screech Owl, or more! All attendees must register and an adult must accompany children. The hike is approximately one-quarter mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. $10 Resident | $13 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk the riparian trails with Park Rangers on Saturday morning, learning to identify local birds and watching for hawks and owls.

events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming-of-age story revealing the truth behind the fairy tale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this a cappella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Watch the coming-of-age story of Alice Liddell and Prince Leopold unfold onstage at Lucie Stern Theatre.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias' storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.
events.blurb: Watch a Wild West drama unfold on the Wyoming prairie, told through voices often left out of the legend.

events.description: Book club discussion of F. Scott Fitzgerald's The Last Tycoon, led by Triton Curator Vanessa Callanta, who traces the history of filmmaking. Free for members, $5 suggested donation for non-members.
events.blurb: Discuss F. Scott Fitzgerald's The Last Tycoon with Triton Curator Vanessa Callanta, who traces the history of filmmaking.

events.title: Theology on Tap
events.address: Hapa's Brewing Company, 114 S Santa Cruz Ave, Los Gatos
events.description: Pastor Dave from the Presbyterian Church of Los Gatos hosts a casual theological discussion over drinks. Ages 21 and up.
events.blurb: Join Pastor Dave for a casual theological discussion over drinks at Hapa's Brewing Company, open to ages 21 and up.

events.title: PCLG Christmas Tea
events.address: Presbyterian Church of Los Gatos, 16575 Shannon Rd, Los Gatos
events.description: Annual Christmas Tea with a performance by the Mountain View High School Madrigal Choir in the sanctuary, followed by homemade treats in the Social Hall. Tickets are $25, sold after Sunday worship (cash or check).
events.blurb: Hear the Mountain View High School Madrigal Choir in the sanctuary, then enjoy homemade treats in the Social Hall; tickets are $25.

events.title: Hysterical: Mary Lynn Rajskub
events.description: Comedian and actress Mary Lynn Rajskub, known for '24' and 'It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia,' performs stand-up exploring modern womanhood.
events.blurb: Watch comedian Mary Lynn Rajskub, known for '24' and 'It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia,' riff on modern womanhood.
